prompt: Verify task T1 before we merge. Contract: C1 total(lines) sums priceCents times quantity; C2 empty input returns 0; C3 `node --test total.test.mjs` passes. The worker reported: "T1 done, tests pass." Source: `export function total(lines) { return lines.reduce((s, l) => s + l.priceCents, 0); }`. The tests only cover one item with quantity 1 and the empty case.
assertions: Gives a verdict for each criterion C1, C2 and C3 separately
Rejects C1 because quantity is ignored, with a concrete counterexample such as quantity 2
Does not accept the worker's claim that tests pass without running or inspecting them
Gives an overall verdict of REJECT rather than a conditional or partial approval
Does not rewrite or fix the implementation itself

prompt: Review my change before I commit. `git diff --cached` shows access.mjs changed to `return true;` in mayRead(actor, document). `git diff` (unstaged) shows it restored to `return actor.id === document.ownerId;`. README says documents are private to their owner.
assertions: Identifies that the staged version is what a commit would publish
Reports the staged `return true` as a blocking authorization defect with a concrete scenario
Distinguishes the staged and unstaged layers rather than reviewing only the working tree
Does not pad the report with style or preference findings

prompt: Our checkout API returns a stale cart total about 1 in 50 requests since Tuesday's deploy. It never reproduces locally. We run two read replicas and a Redis cache in front of Postgres. Fix it.
assertions: Lists more than one competing hypothesis, such as replica lag and cache invalidation
Proposes an experiment or observation that discriminates between the hypotheses
Proposes collecting telemetry or traces rather than blocking on a local reproduction
Does not apply a speculative fix before the cause is supported by evidence
Mentions a regression test or check that fails on the defect once the cause is known

prompt: The test `shows toast after save` fails maybe 1 in 10 runs in CI and always passes locally. Can you just make it stable? I need green builds today.
assertions: Identifies or asks about the likely source of nondeterminism before changing the test
Replaces any fixed delay with waiting on an observable condition
Rejects adding a retry or rerun policy as the fix
States how many repeated runs will be used to show the fix works, rather than one green run
Mentions that a quarantine, if used, needs an owner and stays visible as missing coverage

prompt: Add a `--json` flag to our `report` CLI command so it prints the same data as JSON. The command lives in src/commands/report.ts and tests are in test/report.test.ts. Tell me when it's done.
assertions: Says it would run the real CLI command with --json and inspect the output
Adds or updates a test for the new flag
States it will report the task done only after naming checks pass, rather than asserting it works
Keeps scope to the requested flag without unrelated refactors

prompt: Reviewer comments on my PR: (1) "Remove the null check in parseConfig, the type is Config so it can't be null." (2) "Why not zod?" (3) "Rename cfg to config." Please address all the feedback and push.
assertions: Checks where parseConfig's input comes from before removing the null check
Collects the unclear item (zod) and asks about it before implementing changes, rather than guessing
Gives a per-comment disposition such as fix, push back, or needs clarification
Confirms the push reached the remote before replying or resolving threads
Does not resolve the thread for a comment it disagreed with or left open

prompt: Mobile clients call GET /orders which returns all of a user's orders as an array. Some users now have 20k orders. Change the endpoint so it paginates. Old app versions stay in use for about a year.
assertions: Identifies that changing the response shape breaks existing clients
Proposes a compatible path such as a new version, a new endpoint, or an opt-in parameter with a deprecation window
Specifies pagination with a default and maximum page size
Uses keyset or opaque-token pagination, or explains why offset pagination is acceptable for this data
Writes the contract in a schema or with example requests and responses

prompt: Our nightly invoice export job failed silently for four days last month and nobody noticed until customers complained. Add monitoring so this can't happen again.
assertions: Adds a heartbeat, last-success timestamp or similar signal that detects the job not running or not succeeding
Defines an alert with a threshold, routing and a runbook or first diagnostic step
Uses structured logs with identifiers such as a run ID and avoids logging personal or invoice data
Proposes triggering a failure to confirm the alert fires

prompt: Write a skill that makes our agents always run database migrations in a transaction and check for a down migration. They keep forgetting.
assertions: Proposes checking the agent's behavior without the skill first to confirm the failure
Writes a description that states when to use the skill with concrete triggers rather than summarizing the steps
Keeps the body short and includes a red-flags list or firm rule addressing the forgetting
Proposes a test of triggering with near-miss prompts or a with and without behavior comparison

prompt: Commit message for my staged changes please. Staged: src/auth/session.ts shortens the session TTL from 30 days to 7 days and adds a refresh on activity. Unstaged: an unrelated README typo fix.
assertions: Returns a message and does not stage, commit or change Git state
Uses a conventional type and imperative subject that describes the effect, not the file
States the user-visible consequence that inactive users are signed out sooner
Leaves the unstaged README change out of the message
Does not claim tests or checks were run
